name: Autumn Equinox
title: Autumn Equinox 2026 — the southern crossing
description: On 23 September 2026 at 00:05 UTC, the sun crossed the equator again, heading south, as northern days shortened fastest. Real-time globe, ancient sun-aligned monuments, and pilgrimages from many traditions.
ogDescription: The southern crossing — when northern days shorten fastest and the harvest pilgrimages walk.
twitterDescription: The southern crossing — northern days shortening fastest.
ariaLabel: Where the sun stood at the autumn equinox 2026
noscriptIntro: On 23 September 2026 at 00:05 UTC, the sun crossed the equator again, heading south, as northern days shortened fastest.
articleDescription: On 23 September 2026 at 00:05 UTC, the sun crossed the equator again, heading south, as northern days shortened fastest.
schemaAboutDescription: The astronomical moment when the sun crosses the celestial equator southward, when northern days shorten fastest.

claims.template: The day after this equinox, the sun moved {deg}° south; the day after the June solstice, just {solDeg}°.
claims.source: Sun position: NOAA solar series (Meeus), js/sunpath-math.js. Declination one day after each instant.

claims.template: From the June solstice to this equinox, {days} days and {hours} hours, the longest of the year's four seasons.
claims.source: Turning instants: Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 27.

claims.template: On this equinox, the tip of the staff's shadow at {temple} runs due east, never more than {deg}° off, all day.
claims.source: Sun position: NOAA solar series (Meeus), js/sunpath-math.js. Shadow tip at the temple while the sun is 2° up or more; refraction by Bennett's formula.
